title: jurisdiction rule
description: Structure for the actual jurisdiction-law content that lives in rules/ (not schemas/). deadlineledger.csv's template already fixes five obligation rows (DL-001 to DL-005), one per authority/role pair from brief.md's Authority baseline - this schema is the machine-readable expansion of that same template's clock_rule text column into structured, engine-evaluable logic, so trigger/clock behavior lives in data, not in engine if/else branches.

rule_id.description: Matches deadlineledger.csv obligation_id (DL-001 GDPR Art.33, DL-002 GDPR Art.34, DL-003 NDPA s.40, DL-004 Cal. 1798.82, DL-005 Cal. 1798.82(f) AG sample) so ledger entries trace back to the exact rule that produced them.

trigger_condition.description: Machine-evaluable condition, not free text. Fields depend on rule: e.g. California AG-sample rule needs a population-count threshold; GDPR/NDPA need a risk-threshold flag.

clock_basis.description: Which upstream timestamp starts this obligation's clock. DL-005 (AG sample) must reference 'consumer_notice_utc', not awareness - it is a dependent clock, not a fresh one from awareness.

depends_on_rule_id.description: Set for DL-005, which depends on DL-004's calculated consumer deadline. Null for rules with an independent clock.

feasibility_qualifier.description: True for GDPR Art.33's 'without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours' - the 72-hour figure is a feasibility-qualified ceiling, not an absolute one.

delay_conditions.description: e.g. California's permitted-delay conditions under SB 446. Empty array if none apply.

citation.description: Exact statutory citation as given in brief.md's Authority baseline, e.g. 'GDPR Article 33'.
